chapter: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
title: The Cottontail solo and Hinton's train story
summary: Ben worked up a solo but Duke kept the check tape take; Hinton heard Ben play it on a train.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Did I tell this the last time, the story about "Cotton-tail", that classic solo? He'd worked this solo up, he wrote the piece and Duke wrote an arrangement for him, he had his ready, with a solo for it, and they'd go down to the studio and they're making a check tape. And so he lays down any old solo for that. Duke says, "that's it." He said, "no, no, that wasn't the solo." Duke says, "that's it." No, you don't understand, I've got a solo." Duke said, that was it. The funny part was the solo he plays, which -- I'm sorry I never heard the one he worked up, if he thought it was better. It would have been something to hear.

I'd like to add something to that. Just before they made that recording, Cab Calloway's band and Duke Ellington's band met someplace in the Midwest we played, and they hooked the two trains together, Duke Ellington's car and Cab Calloway's car together, and like they were going to Milwaukee and we were going on to Omaha. / So for a few hours we had the biggest and the drunkenest time anybody could have. And Ben happened to be in Cab's band with me, because Ben was

one of the guys who helped get me into Cab's band before he left and went with Duke, we were so glad to see each other. And he told me, he said, you know, we're going to record and I'm going to do a solo, I've got a tune I wrote. And I said, yes, that's great. He said, Duke's going to let me make a record. And I said, that's great. What is it, what did you name it? You know what he'd named it? "Shucking and Stiffing."

And he sat there and he played, I believe, that solo that you didn't hear. On the train, we were sitting there and he played, and it was fantastic. I realize what the tune was, which of course, you know what the tune was, the basic chord changes. And then when a record came out I saw "Cottontail," Ben Webster, I think it was one of the first things he did as a special. And I said, that ain't the one that Ben played for me.

That's right, yeah. I guess he named that after Johnny Hodges then, because they called Hodges "Rabbit," and I always figured, because I know he admired Hodges -- he didn't like him but he admired him.
